measurements.name: cuda.libcudart_resolved_by_loader
measurements.note: THE DECIDING FACT: this is the libcudart a native dlopen finds, because ldconfig's cache is consulted when LD_LIBRARY_PATH does not name one. It is not the library the CUDA toolkit directory holds

measurements.name: cuda.libcudart_exports_provider_symbol
measurements.note: the reason the registration fails: the resolved library exports the symbol the CUDA provider needs 0 time(s). A count of zero is the failure, and it is why addCUDA() throws

measurements.name: cuda.libcudart_with_provider_symbol
measurements.command: find <the project's virtualenv nvidia lib dirs> -name libcudart.so.12
measurements.note: the library that DOES export the symbol; naming it on LD_LIBRARY_PATH is the whole fix

measurements.name: onnxruntime.available_providers
measurements.note: the providers the ONNX Runtime build OFFERS, read from a real run of the Java API MATRIX uses. A provider being listed here is NOT evidence that it was registered for a session

measurements.name: onnxruntime.addcuda_without_ld_library_path
measurements.command: the same probe with no LD_LIBRARY_PATH
measurements.note: this IS the MATRIX configuration: matrix-core/build.gradle builds java.library.path, but a native dlopen consults LD_LIBRARY_PATH, so the loader finds the distro's libcudart and the registration fails

measurements.name: onnxruntime.addcuda_with_ld_library_path
measurements.command: the same probe with LD_LIBRARY_PATH naming the project's virtualenv CUDA libraries
measurements.note: the same probe, the same jars, one environment variable added

measurements.name: matrix.gpu_execution_verified
measurements.note: MATRIX does not execute on the GPU: the adapter requests CUDA inside a try/catch whose catch logs a warning and continues (lines 104-114), and the diagnostic that reports the active provider is a hardcoded CPUExecutionProvider (lines 118-123). The probe establishes that the hardware is present and the registration FAILS in MATRIX's own configuration; the source establishes what MATRIX does with that failure

measurements.name: matrix.gpu_provider_diagnostic_is_hardcoded
measurements.note: activeProviders is assigned a one-element array unconditionally, so any dashboard reading it sees 'CPU' whether the GPU is in use or not

measurements.name: benchmark.gpu_forward_speedup
measurements.note: REPORTED, NOT REPRODUCED BY THIS PROBE: 191.367 ms per forward on the CPU against 15.190 ms on the CUDA, for models/onnx/qwen05b/model.onnx at sequence length 32, 10 iterations after one warm-up. This probe runs no benchmark by design
